Examples ​

Every example lives in the repository's examples/ directory as a .tui, a .tcss, and sample data, most with a small Go host. Each picture is rendered from tuimark play on those files (the command is in its title bar), so you can reproduce it exactly. Screens that come in two palettes follow this site's light or dark mode.

tuimark play runs no host program, so these pictures show the sample data and what the built-in keys do. The apps' own actions, such as sending a request or moving a card, need the Go host.

The first nine examples move on their own, so their pictures are animations: each Go app has a -demo flag that replays a scripted session on a fake clock with a fixed seed and prints every frame, and the site turns those frames into an animated SVG. Use the button in the title bar to pause one; with reduced motion turned on in your system settings, they start paused.

To run them, clone the repository and build:

sh
git clone https://github.com/abdul-hamid-achik/tuimark
cd tuimark
go build -o bin/tuimark ./cmd/tuimark
go build -o bin/monitor ./examples/monitor
./bin/monitor

snake ​

examples/snake is a playable Snake. The game loop is an Every tick whose interval is the snake's speed: each food raises the level, and the tick re-arms itself faster. -autopilot (or A while playing) hands the wheel to a small search that steers to the food.

sh
go build -o bin/snake ./examples/snake
./bin/snake                      # arrows, hjkl or wasd steer; space pauses
./bin/snake -autopilot           # watch it play

chess ​

examples/chess is chess with a real engine behind it. Move generation is checked against the published perft counts, moves go in by mouse, by cursor, or typed as SAN or UCI, and games load and save as FEN and PGN. The engine is a small alpha-beta search with six levels; it thinks in a goroutine and hands its move back through Batch, so the board never freezes while it searches. You can play it, give it a friend's seat, let it play itself, or step through a game in review.

sh
go build -o bin/chess ./examples/chess
./bin/chess                      # you play White against level 3
./bin/chess -mode 2p -clock 5+0  # two players, five minutes each
./bin/chess -pgn game.pgn        # step through a game

tetris ​

examples/tetris is a falling-blocks game with the modern rules: SRS rotation with wall kicks, a 7-bag, a hold slot, a ghost piece, lock delay, T-spins, and combos. One fixed Every tick drives gravity, the lock delay, and the line-clear flash on a game clock, so a level change takes effect on the next tick. a hands the game to an autopilot that weighs every placement.

sh
go build -o bin/tetris ./examples/tetris
./bin/tetris                     # arrows or hjkl move, space drops, x/z rotate, c holds
./bin/tetris -autopilot          # watch it play

minesweeper ​

examples/minesweeper is Minesweeper on the three classic boards or a custom one. The first reveal always opens a region, a revealed number chords its neighbors, and f switches the left click to flagging, since only the left button reaches the document. The 480 cells of the largest board are static elements generated into app.tui, so a click names its cell, and if shows the ones the current board uses.

sh
go build -o bin/minesweeper ./examples/minesweeper
./bin/minesweeper                       # beginner; 1, 2, 3 switch boards
./bin/minesweeper -level expert
./bin/minesweeper -cols 20 -rows 12 -mines 30

sudoku ​

examples/sudoku generates puzzles with exactly one solution and grades them by the techniques they need, from singles to X-wings. It has notes, hints, a check, undo and redo, and a number pad you can click. The notes of the cell under the cursor show as a 3×3 grid in the side panel, since a one-row cell has no room for them.

sh
go build -o bin/sudoku ./examples/sudoku
./bin/sudoku -difficulty hard
./bin/sudoku -puzzle 53..7....6..195....98....6.8...6...34..8.3..17...2...6.6....28....419..5....8..79

2048 ​

examples/2048 is the sliding-tiles game on a 3×3 to 6×6 board, with undo, a win dialog that lets you keep going, and an autopilot that searches a couple of moves ahead. Merged tiles pop and the new tile lights up for a moment: the move sets the highlight, and an Every tick clears it.

sh
go build -o bin/2048 ./examples/2048
./bin/2048                       # arrows, hjkl or wasd slide; u undoes
./bin/2048 -size 5 -autopilot

pipeline ​

examples/pipeline is a CI run in the terminal: stages of parallel jobs with spinners, progress bars and timers, and the selected job's log streaming into a <scroll stick="bottom">. A flaky test fails on the first run; r retries it and the later stages go on.

sh
go build -o bin/pipeline ./examples/pipeline
./bin/pipeline                   # j/k pick a job, r retries, R reruns, c cancels
./bin/pipeline -speed 8          # simulated seconds per real second

music ​

examples/music is a music player with no audio: a library table with a filter, a queue, albums, and a now-playing panel whose spectrum visualizer is a six-row <sparkline> the tick feeds.

sh
go build -o bin/music ./examples/music
./bin/music                      # space plays and pauses, n/p skip, a queues
./bin/music -speed 8             # run the playback clock faster

pomodoro ​

examples/pomodoro is a Pomodoro timer and a clock in big block digits. The digits are one derived string per frame shown in a <text> (the blinking colon is drawn into that string), and the phase colors and the pulse of the last ten seconds are class: guards on values the tick computes.

sh
go build -o bin/pomodoro ./examples/pomodoro
./bin/pomodoro -start            # space starts and pauses, s skips, 2 shows the clock
./bin/pomodoro -work 50m -short 10m

monitor studio ​

examples/monitor is a system monitor's studio view, and the showcase for everything version="2" adds: nine tabs, a panel grid with gauges and sparklines, a scrolling grid of per-core bars, a process table with sortable columns and multi-select, a filter input, kill confirmations, a detail modal, settings that switch the mouse and the theme, and a hint bar built from the keymap. theme="auto" picks its palette from the terminal.

The Go host has no layout, width, padding, truncation, or column code. It runs a seeded fake collector and handles the named actions: sorting (the sort arrow in the header is data), filtering, kill and force kill, the pinned detail, and the settings.

sh
./bin/monitor                    # run it
./bin/monitor --theme light      # Set("@theme", "light") before Run
./bin/monitor --dump 120x30      # print Dump() as JSON instead

logs ​

examples/logs is a live log viewer, like tail -f: lines stream in, colored by level, and the view follows the end until you scroll up to read. A filter input and the 1-4 level toggles narrow what is shown, and a sparkline tracks lines per second.

The host streams lines with Every, which appends them in one Batch per tick, and Derive keeps the filtered lines and the counts, so the markup has no expressions. -follow FILE tails a real file instead of the built-in generator.

sh
go build -o bin/logs ./examples/logs
./bin/logs                       # a seeded fake API service
./bin/logs -follow app.log       # tail a real file

tasks ​

examples/tasks is a kanban board: three lanes of cards that you move, reorder, mark, create, edit, and delete from the keyboard, with a filter over every lane.

New and edited cards go through a form modal; deleting asks first. -file board.json keeps the board in a file, and a failed save shows in the status line through RunWith's OnError.

sh
go build -o bin/tasks ./examples/tasks
./bin/tasks -file board.json

gitui ​

examples/gitui is a small git client in the spirit of tig and lazygit: staged and unstaged files with a diff preview, the log with each commit's detail, and the branches with a checkout confirmation.

The log is a table whose <column priority> values decide which columns go first on a narrow terminal, and each tab has its own keys through <keymap when>. By default it shows a sample repository; -repo PATH reads a real one with git, read-only unless you also pass -write.

sh
go build -o bin/gitui ./examples/gitui
./bin/gitui                      # the sample repository
./bin/gitui -repo .              # this repository, read-only

http ​

examples/http is an HTTP API client, like Postman: a collection of saved requests, an editor for the method, URL, headers, and body, and the response with its status, timing, body, and headers.

Requests run in a goroutine and land with one Batch; while one is in flight, an Every tick animates the spinner and the elapsed time, and esc cancels it. Without -base, the collection targets a fake API the host serves in process, so it works offline.

sh
go build -o bin/http ./examples/http
./bin/http                       # against the built-in fake API
./bin/http -base https://api.example.com

inbox ​

examples/inbox is a ticket inbox: a search input, a list bound to an array, and a detail pane that shows the selected ticket, in a version="1" document.

The host wires three actions: open shows the selected ticket, search filters the list, and quit stops.

dashboard ​

examples/dashboard is a deploy dashboard with two screens, a pipeline list, a progress bar, buttons, a scrolling log, and a confirm modal. Header and footer are docked.

The Logs and Back buttons switch screens with Set("@screen", …); Deploy (or d on it) opens the confirmation. Once confirmed, the host runs a fake deploy in a goroutine that advances the steps and the progress bar with Set, which is safe from any goroutine.

agent ​

examples/agent is a small, real coding-agent chat: a transcript, a composer, tool activity and touched files, plan and build modes, and approval modals for edits and commands. It talks to a scripted provider or a local Ollama model, and has a headless mode.

The whole view is agent.tui and agent.tcss; the Go code supplies data and named actions only. See its README for the providers, the workspace sandbox, and the flags.

sh
go build -o bin/agent ./examples/agent
./bin/agent --demo-workspace ./demo-workspace

unicode ​

examples/unicode checks the hard part of terminal text: CJK characters two columns wide, emoji, and combining accents, in a list, in wrapped text, and next to borders.

Widths are measured by grapheme cluster, a cluster is never split when text wraps or is cut, and borders stay aligned. Its dump has "wide": true, and --cells maps every column.

spike ​

examples/spike is where Tuimark started: five tags, two bordered boxes, and a status line, with no stylesheet. Its goldens are frozen, so a change to its geometry is a runtime regression, never an update.

Write your own ​

Start from getting started, borrow freely from these files, and keep the widgets page open.

logs, tasks, gitui, http, snake, pipeline, music, and pomodoro also ship a mock.json, so you can try their views in the terminal with no Go at all through tuimark run:

sh
tuimark run examples/tasks/app.tui --data examples/tasks/sample.json --mock examples/tasks/mock.json
